diagnoses.lesson: Define arithmetic bounds and validation precedence before implementation; preserve input order, and round each measurement at the specified stage.
Model each operation’s ordering explicitly: admit time, apply required expiry, then validate and mutate; keep scoped data, snapshots, and deadlines independently represented.
Translate every requirement into explicit validation order, output invariants, and edge-case checks before choosing an algorithm; preserve original input indices throughout.

diagnoses.bug: The specification couples brace-boundary detection with escape decoding, making malformed and selected defaults easy to parse inconsistently; wildcard offsets also require tracking the decoded output byte position as fragments append.
diagnoses.lesson: Separate source scanning from output construction: preserve original byte offsets for errors, and track decoded output positions independently when appending transformed fragments.

diagnoses.bug: The contract combines precise byte-level validation, stable age ordering, indexed updates, atomic failures, and transactional merge semantics. A likely implementation bug is mutating or partially transferring state before all validation, lookup, or collision checks have succeeded.
diagnoses.lesson: Validate inputs and preflight every failure condition before mutation; preserve stable metadata explicitly, and define ordering with a complete comparator rather than incidental container order.
Track streaming state and physical input offsets across chunks; apply validation in the specified order before emitting results.
Keep each ordering structure aligned with its own contract, and make failures preserve the failed item while committing only completed work.
Model event-driven systems as explicit ordered phases, and validate inputs before execution while checking arithmetic exactly when operations occur.
Translate every requirement into explicit validation order, stable traversal order, and edge-case behavior before implementing the core transformation.

diagnoses.bug: The validation order is easy to get wrong: range-checking during the initial scan can mask a later invalid byte, while checksum mismatches can mask leading-zero or range errors.
diagnoses.lesson: Separate parsing into ordered validation phases, then use checked arithmetic at every prefix so error precedence and overflow behavior stay deterministic.
Validate input in the specified order and coordinate system before normalizing it; keep delimiter parsing scoped to its component and preserve optional-value distinctions.
For strict parsers, separate whole-input lexical validation, delimiter checks, and dictionary validation from arithmetic; only then compute safely and compare against the canonical serialization.

lessons: Translate requirements into explicit validation order, output invariants, stable ordering, and edge cases before choosing an algorithm.
Validate inputs and preflight failure conditions before mutation; preserve original indices, offsets, metadata, and optional-value distinctions explicitly.
Model operations as ordered phases, applying admission, expiry, validation, and mutation exactly when specified.
Use checked arithmetic at each required operation or prefix, and define bounds, rounding stages, and overflow precedence explicitly.
Separate scanning and parsing phases from output construction; track source positions and transformed output positions independently.
Track streaming state and physical input offsets across chunks; emit results only after the required validation succeeds.
Keep each ordering structure aligned with its contract, using complete comparators instead of incidental container order.
Preserve failed items and commit only completed work; represent scoped data, snapshots, and deadlines independently.
